quotes.text: Task data originates from MIMIC-IV v2.2, a PhysioNet snapshot from January 2023.
Each task record preserves the source patient identifier, enabling complete traceability from any task back to its underlying patient record.

rationale: The paper names the dataset and version (MIMIC-IV v2.2), the platform (PhysioNet) and a snapshot date, and states that each task keeps the source patient identifier. This gives a route from task to source record, so all anchor parts are present.

quotes.text: All patient records originate from a de-identified hospital database collected during routine care between 2008 and 2019.
the data are released under terms separate from the MIT code licence.
the source institution's review board determined that the study qualified for a waiver of consent.

rationale: Origin, collection setting, data terms (DUA, credentialed access, separate from the MIT code licence) and an ethics determination with consent waiver are all stated in S1.

searched: S1 (dataset, Q&A design and evaluation sections, appendices), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4 and S5. The paper gives case and question counts but no descriptive statistics of key patient features, no stated sampling rule, and no comparison to a target population.

searched: S1 (societal impacts, evaluation, appendices), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. The only mention of a safety test suite and a bias test is a code comment in S4 (agent_eval/notes.py), which cannot count as reporting under G1a. S1 and S2 report no dedicated unsafe-output or bias test.

quotes.text: A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.
Measurement of verbatim overlap with public web corpora revealed zero exact matches between test tasks and public sources.

rationale: Developer-side controls are stated (gated test split, private held-out split, canary string), together with a measured overlap check against public web corpora that found zero exact matches.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment, so answers cannot leak through external search.

rationale: S1 states that answers cannot leak through external search and that held-out labels are kept off public surfaces. It does not state that the agent cannot reach ground truth at run time with a named mechanism. The no-network-path statement exists only in an S4 comment, which does not count.

quotes.text: The environment is frozen at release: the database snapshot, the software image and the simulated-patient language model are all pinned to fixed versions
no external service is called at evaluation time other than the model under test.

contradiction_quotes.text: no external service is called at evaluation time other than the model under test.
You also have access to PUBMED that you can use to query articles that may potentially be relevant to the patient history.

rationale: S1 reports data, software image and simulator pinned with no live external call other than the model under test, so the score is 2. The agent prompt and tool code give agents live PubMed querying, which conflicts with the no-external-service claim, so a contradiction flag is set.

quotes.text: we ran a scripted reference solution for each task through the grader; all 120 reference solutions were graded correct.

rationale: A scripted reference solution was run through the grader for each task and the result (120 of 120 correct) is reported.

quotes.text: Writes are executed against a sandboxed copy of the record, and unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score.
Grading operates on the final environment state.

rationale: Tasks involve write actions, so the NA clause does not apply. Grading reads the final environment state and unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised, which means out-of-scope changes are detected as well as required ones.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks, and the chance success rate for each metric is reported in the appendix.

rationale: An empirical random-agent success rate (3.1%) and a chance rate per metric are reported.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks

rationale: A random-action agent's result is reported over tasks as a whole (3.1%), with per-metric chance rates in the appendix. No per-task-family breakdown is shown, so coverage of all tasks is read from the aggregate statement.

quotes.text: Grader validation tested 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, yielding 1% false acceptance and 2% false rejection rates.

rationale: The benchmark validates its own grader on injected correct and incorrect outcomes and reports false acceptance and false rejection rates.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

contradiction_quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times
Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds; the temperature was set to 0.7

rationale: S1 states temperature 0, a fixed seed and a three-run policy, which meets the anchor. A code comment in S4 gives five runs, independent seeds and temperature 0.7, and gpt_4o.py uses temperature=0.2, so a contradiction flag is set.

quotes.text: test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test (p = 0.02).

rationale: 95% bootstrap CIs are reported for all model scores and the top-two model difference is tested with a paired permutation test.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

contradiction_quotes.text: each task is run three times
Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds; the temperature was set to 0.7

rationale: S1 gives a run count (three) and seed plus temperature, so elements (i) and (ii) are present. Independence of runs is stated only in an S4 comment, so (iii) is absent. The S4 comment also gives five runs at temperature 0.7, which contradicts S1.

quotes.text: We report 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks, so the resampling unit is the task
where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead to account for clustering.

rationale: CIs are reported on headline scores, the resampling unit is named, and clustering of tasks within patients is handled by patient-level resampling.

searched: S1 (evaluation, appendices D to G), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4 and S5. S1 gives a run count but reports no score variation across reruns, no all-runs metric, and no action- or state-level agreement across reruns.

quotes.text: snapshot identifiers gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022
temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens; all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0.

contradiction_quotes.text: temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens

rationale: S1 gives snapshot model identifiers, decoding parameters and a harness release matching the reported numbers. The GPT-4o evaluation code uses temperature=0.2 and max_tokens=1024, which conflicts with S1, so a contradiction flag is set. The model identifiers themselves do not differ between S1 and S4.

quotes.text: The write actions that change patient state (medication orders, notes and messages) are listed in a table.
When a drug name match is identified, the corresponding description is returned to the LLM

rationale: Tools use a text-command protocol, so NA does not apply. No schema or enforced grammar is given in S1 and failure returns are not documented. Write actions are listed and sandboxed, and S1 says the agent prompt states that writes are sandboxed, but the S5 prompts shown in the packet do not show this text.

quotes.text: We ran conformance tests confirming that each tool behaves as documented.
Two tools are simulated stubs that return fixed placeholder responses; this is disclosed in the paper
also stated in the tool descriptions shown to the agent.

rationale: S1 reports conformance tests, discloses two simulated stub tools, and states the disclosure is in the tool descriptions shown to the agent. The S5 prompts in the packet do not contain this text, but they are partial and the packet does not show the opposite.

quotes.text: The write actions that change patient state (medication orders, notes and messages) are listed in a table.
Writes are executed against a sandboxed copy of the record, and unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score.
The agent prompt states that writes are sandboxed.

rationale: The write actions are listed, they run against a sandboxed copy, and unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised. S1 states that the agent prompt says writes are sandboxed, so S5 reach is recorded as true on that report. The S5 prompt text in the packet does not show that statement.

quotes.text: Grading operates on the final environment state.
Grader validation tested 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, yielding 1% false acceptance and 2% false rejection rates.

rationale: The grader input is the final environment state and an LLM comparator is also mentioned. No rationale is needed for state grading, so element (ii) is not shown. Validation on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes with per-class error rates is reported, which gives 2.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment, so answers cannot leak through external search.
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.

contradiction_quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs
You also have access to PUBMED that you can use to query articles that may potentially be relevant to the patient history.

rationale: S1 reports controls on web and retrieval leakage, a private held-out split with hidden labels, and a canary string, so all three elements are present. The agent prompt gives live PubMed querying, which conflicts with the no-web-access claim, so a contradiction flag is set.

quotes.text: We report accuracy per task family (diagnosis, ordering and documentation tasks) and per patient subgroup by sex and race
each table lists the number of cases in every slice.

rationale: S1 states results per task family and per sex and race subgroup, with the number of cases listed for every slice. The task-family names differ from the paper's own task axes, but only what is reported is scored.

quotes.text: The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database.
Their use was approved under a data use agreement requiring credentialed access and de-identification by the safe harbour method
the data are released under terms separate from the MIT code licence.

rationale: The records are stated to be real and de-identified, governance is given (DUA, credentialed access, safe harbour de-identification), and the data terms are stated separately from the MIT code licence.
